title: Add Validation, Error Handling, and OpenAPI Documentation
description: Strengthen API robustness with request validation, structured errors, logging, and generated API docs.
details:
Deliverables:
- Shared validation layer using Zod + `express-zod-api` or custom middleware.
- Centralized error formatter mapping domain errors to HTTP codes.
- OpenAPI spec coverage for all endpoints with `@asteasolutions/zod-to-openapi` to generate `openapi.yaml` and serve via Swagger UI on `/docs`.
Pseudo-code:
```
const createServiceSchema = z.object({ title: z.string().min(3), ... });
app.post('/api/services', validate(createServiceSchema), asyncHandler(createService));
```
Implementation notes:
- Instrument structured logging for validation failures.
- Provide response envelope spec for consistency (`{ data, meta }`).
- Document rate limiting and auth requirements within OpenAPI.
testStrategy: Unit tests for validation schemas; snapshot test validating OpenAPI generation; integration test ensuring invalid payload returns 422 with error details.

tasks.title: Establish Design System Foundation in Tailwind and Install Dependencies
tasks.description: Extend the existing Tailwind CSS configuration to include the new design system (colors, typography, spacing) and install all required new dependencies for advanced animations and interactions.
tasks.details:
1. **Install Dependencies**: Run `npm install framer-motion@^11 lucide-react@^0 lenis@^1 react-intersection-observer@^9 @react-three/fiber@^8 @react-three/drei@^9 three@^0.16 lottie-react@^2`. 
2. **Update Tailwind Config**: Modify `tailwind.config.ts` to extend `theme` with the new color palette (primary blue gradient, secondary purple, neon accents), typography (Inter, JetBrains Mono), and spacing scale. 
3. **Create Utilities**: Add custom utilities for glassmorphism (`.glass`, `.glass-dark`), neumorphism shadows, and gradient text. 
4. **Animation Variants**: Create `/apps/web/src/components/animations/variants.ts` to define reusable Framer Motion variants (fadeIn, slideUp, scale, stagger) with specified durations and easing.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that all new dependencies are installed and the application builds successfully. Check that new color, font, and spacing utilities are available and can be applied to components. Create a test page to render elements with the new styles and Framer Motion variants to confirm they work as expected.

tasks.title: Build Core UI Component Library
tasks.description: Develop a set of reusable, accessible, and animated core components based on the new design system. This includes buttons, cards, inputs, modals, and other fundamental UI elements.
tasks.details:
Create each component in its own file under `/apps/web/src/components/ui/`. 
- **Button.tsx**: Use `cva` (class-variance-authority) to create variants (primary, secondary, ghost, neon, gradient). Integrate Framer Motion for hover/press animations and a ripple effect. 
- **Card.tsx**: A flexible card component with props for animated hover effects (lift, glow, 3D tilt). 
- **Input.tsx**: Implement a text input with a floating label effect and focus animations on the border/label. 
- **Modal.tsx**: A dialog component with a backdrop blur effect (`backdrop-blur-sm`) and a scale/fade-in animation. 
- **Other Components**: Develop Tooltip, Toast, Spinners, and Progress indicators using `lucide-react` for icons.
tasks.testStrategy: Use Storybook or a dedicated test page to render and test each component in isolation. Verify all variants and states (hover, focus, disabled). Check for accessibility compliance (keyboard navigation, ARIA attributes). Test responsiveness on different screen sizes.

tasks.title: Implement Sticky Header and Animated Footer
tasks.description: Build the main layout components, including a sticky navigation header with smooth-scrolling links and an animated footer with social media icons.
tasks.details:
1. **Header**: Create `/apps/web/src/components/layout/Header.tsx`. Make it sticky to the top. Implement a smooth scroll to section IDs. Use `useInView` or a scroll listener to highlight the active section link. For mobile, create a hamburger menu that triggers a slide-out navigation pane using Framer Motion's `AnimatePresence`. 
2. **Footer**: Create `/apps/web/src/components/layout/Footer.tsx`. Add animated links (underline effect on hover) and social media icons from `lucide-react` that scale or glow on hover. 
3. **Layout Integration**: Update the main layout file (`/apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx`) to include the new Header and Footer components.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify the header remains fixed at the top on scroll. Test smooth scrolling to all sections on the homepage. Confirm the active link highlighting works correctly. Test the mobile hamburger menu animation and functionality on various device widths. Check footer link animations.

subtasks.title: Create Basic Sticky Header Component Structure
subtasks.description: Develop the initial file and structure for the `Header.tsx` component, including basic navigation links. Implement sticky positioning to ensure it remains fixed at the top of the viewport during scroll.
subtasks.details: Create the file at `/apps/web/src/components/layout/Header.tsx`. Use Tailwind CSS classes for styling (e.g., `sticky top-0 z-50 bg-background/80 backdrop-blur-sm`). Add a `nav` element containing a list of placeholder links that will later be used for smooth scrolling. Style using the project's design tokens.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify the header component renders correctly. Scroll the page to confirm the header remains fixed at the top. Check that the background blur effect works as expected.

subtasks.title: Implement Mobile Hamburger Menu with Slide-Out Panel
subtasks.description: Enhance the `Header.tsx` component with a responsive hamburger menu for mobile views. The menu button will toggle a slide-out navigation panel using animations from Framer Motion.
subtasks.details: Use a `useState` hook to manage the open/closed state of the mobile menu. Use Tailwind's responsive prefixes (e.g., `md:hidden`) to show the hamburger icon on mobile and the full nav on desktop. Wrap the mobile navigation panel with Framer Motion's `AnimatePresence` and use `motion` components to animate its entry and exit (e.g., slide from right).
subtasks.testStrategy: On a small screen width, verify the hamburger menu icon is visible and the desktop navigation is hidden. Test that clicking the icon opens and closes the slide-out panel smoothly. Ensure links within the panel are clickable.

subtasks.title: Add Smooth Scrolling and Active Link Highlighting
subtasks.description: Implement smooth scrolling for navigation links to target specific section IDs on the page. Add a visual indicator to highlight the navigation link corresponding to the section currently in the viewport.
subtasks.details: Create a reusable component for navigation links that handles the smooth scroll logic on click. Use the `react-intersection-observer` package's `useInView` hook on each content section of the main page. Based on which section's `inView` status is true, update a shared state to apply an 'active' class (e.g., different text color or an underline) to the corresponding link in the header.
subtasks.testStrategy: Click on each navigation link and verify it smoothly scrolls to the correct section. Scroll the page manually and confirm that the active link in the header updates correctly as different sections enter the viewport.

subtasks.title: Build Animated Footer Component with Social Links
subtasks.description: Create the `Footer.tsx` component, which will include animated navigation links and social media icons from `lucide-react` with hover effects.
subtasks.details: Create the file at `/apps/web/src/components/layout/Footer.tsx`. Add a list of footer links and use CSS pseudo-elements (`::after`) and Tailwind's `group-hover` utilities to create an animated underline effect. Import icons (e.g., `Github`, `Twitter`, `Linkedin`) from `lucide-react` and wrap them in `motion.a` tags from Framer Motion to add a `scale` or `opacity` change on hover.
subtasks.testStrategy: Render the footer and verify all links and icons are present. Hover over the navigation links to check for the animated underline effect. Hover over each social media icon to confirm its scale or glow animation triggers correctly.

subtasks.title: Integrate Header and Footer into Root Layout
subtasks.description: Update the main application layout file (`/apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx`) to include the newly created Header and Footer components, ensuring they are displayed correctly across all pages.
subtasks.details: Open `/apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx`. Import the `Header` from `~/components/layout/Header` and `Footer` from `~/components/layout/Footer`. Place the `<Header />` component inside the `<body>` tag, before the `{children}` prop. Place the `<Footer />` component after the `{children}` prop. Ensure the main content area is properly spaced to avoid overlapping with the fixed header.
subtasks.testStrategy: Navigate to multiple pages of the application and verify that the Header and Footer components are consistently present. Check the page for any layout issues, such as content being obscured by the sticky header or footer.

tasks.title: Develop Interactive Hero Section with 3D Background
tasks.description: Create the homepage's hero section, focusing on the 'wow factor' with a Three.js particle background, floating 3D shapes, a typewriter headline effect, and interactive CTA buttons.
tasks.details:
1. **3D Scene**: Create a component `HeroBackground.tsx` using `@react-three/fiber`. Use `@react-three/drei`'s `Stars` or a custom `Points` geometry for the particle effect. Add several `Mesh` objects with `IcosahedronGeometry` for the floating shapes, animating their position and rotation. 
2. **Typewriter Effect**: Implement a custom React hook `useTypewriter(text, speed)` that returns the animated string, or use a lightweight library. 
3. **Animated Counters**: Use `framer-motion`'s `animate` function to animate numbers from 0 to a target value, triggered by `react-intersection-observer`. 
4. **CTA Buttons**: Use the `Button` component from the core library (Task 2) with `glow` and `ripple` effects enabled. Implement a loading state for the button.
tasks.testStrategy: Test the hero section on various devices and browsers to ensure 3D animation performance is smooth (aim for 60fps). Verify the typewriter effect plays correctly. Check that the counters animate into view. Test the CTA button's hover, click, and loading states.

subtasks.title: Create 3D Particle and Shape Background Component
subtasks.description: Develop the `HeroBackground.tsx` component using @react-three/fiber to render the animated 3D background. This includes a particle field and floating geometric shapes.
subtasks.details: Create a new component at `apps/web/src/components/three/HeroBackground.tsx`. Inside a Canvas, use `@react-three/drei`'s `Stars` component for the particle effect. Add several `Mesh` elements with `IcosahedronGeometry` and `MeshStandardMaterial`. Use the `useFrame` hook to animate the rotation and position of the shapes to create a floating effect.
subtasks.testStrategy: Render the component in isolation on a test page. Verify that the stars are visible and the shapes are animating smoothly. Check performance to ensure it maintains a high frame rate.

subtasks.title: Implement `useTypewriter` Custom Hook
subtasks.description: Create a custom React hook `useTypewriter` that animates a string of text, returning the updated text at a specified interval.
subtasks.details: Create a new file `apps/web/srcs/hooks/useTypewriter.ts`. The hook should accept a string and a typing speed (ms) as arguments. It will use `useState` and `useEffect` with `setTimeout` to incrementally build the string and return the current state. Ensure the hook has a cleanup function to clear the timeout.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test the hook in a simple component to verify it types out the full provided text correctly and at the expected speed. Check that the animation restarts if the input text changes.

subtasks.title: Build the Main Hero Section Layout Component
subtasks.description: Create the main `Hero.tsx` component that will serve as the container for the hero section, structuring the layout and integrating the 3D background.
subtasks.details: Create `apps/web/src/components/sections/Hero.tsx`. This component will have a full-height container. It will render the `HeroBackground` component with `position: absolute` and `z-index: -1`. It will also define the main content area using a centered Flexbox or Grid layout to prepare for the text and buttons.
subtasks.testStrategy: Render the `Hero` component on the homepage (`apps/web/src/app/page.tsx`). Verify that the 3D background is correctly displayed behind the content area and that the layout is responsive.

subtasks.title: Integrate Typewriter Headline and Interactive CTA Buttons
subtasks.description: Add the main headline using the `useTypewriter` hook and the Call-to-Action buttons using the core UI library's `Button` component.
subtasks.details: In `Hero.tsx`, call the `useTypewriter` hook to animate the H1 headline text. Below the headline, add a paragraph for the sub-headline. Import the `Button` component from `apps/web/src/components/ui/button.tsx` and add two instances. Use the appropriate variants (e.g., 'gradient', 'neon') as defined in the design system and Task 2. Implement hover/glow effects and a loading state.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify the headline animates correctly on page load. Test the CTA buttons' hover, active, and focus states. Ensure the glow and ripple effects are present. Trigger a mock loading state on click to test its visual appearance.

subtasks.title: Develop and Integrate Animated Counters Component
subtasks.description: Create a component for animated statistic counters that animate from zero to a target number when they scroll into view.
subtasks.details: Create a component `AnimatedCounters.tsx` in `apps/web/src/components/sections/`. Use `react-intersection-observer`'s `useInView` hook to trigger the animation. Use `framer-motion`'s `animate` function to tween the numbers. The component should accept an array of objects, each with a label and a target value. Integrate this component into the `Hero.tsx` layout.
subtasks.testStrategy: Place the component in the hero section. Scroll down and back up to ensure the animation triggers only when the component is in the viewport. Verify the numbers animate smoothly to their final target values.

tasks.title: Build Advanced Scroll-Based Animations and Page Transitions
tasks.description: Integrate a smooth scrolling library (Lenis) and implement various scroll-triggered animations like parallax, reveals, and staggers. Set up global page transitions for a seamless user experience.
tasks.details:
1. **Smooth Scrolling**: Integrate `lenis` by wrapping the main app layout. Create a React context to provide the Lenis instance throughout the app for programmatic scrolling if needed. 
2. **Scroll-Triggered Animations**: Use `react-intersection-observer`'s `useInView` hook to trigger Framer Motion animations as elements enter the viewport. Apply this to sections, lists, and individual components. For list items, use Framer Motion's `staggerChildren` prop on the parent container. 
3. **Page Transitions**: In the root `layout.tsx`, wrap the `{children}` prop with Framer Motion's `<AnimatePresence mode='wait'>`. On each page component's root element, add a `<motion.div>` with `initial`, `animate`, and `exit` props to define slide, fade, or scale transitions.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify smooth scrolling is active on all pages. Scroll up and down the homepage to confirm that elements animate into view correctly and without jank. Navigate between different pages to test that the enter and exit animations are smooth and consistent. Check for performance issues, especially on lower-end devices.

tasks.title: Construct Services and Case Studies Sections
tasks.description: Develop the 'Services' and 'Case Studies' sections for the homepage, featuring interactive cards with 3D tilt effects, filtering, and a lightbox gallery.
tasks.details:
1. **Services Section**: Create service cards with a 3D tilt effect on hover using Framer Motion's `useMotionValue` and `useTransform` hooks to map mouse position to `rotateX` and `rotateY`. Implement a filter system using `useState` to manage the active category and Framer Motion's `AnimatePresence` to animate items in and out. 
2. **Case Studies Section**: Build interactive cards that use a flip animation (`rotateY: 180`) on hover to reveal details. Integrate a 'Before/After' slider component. Clicking a card should open a modal-based lightbox gallery for images.
tasks.testStrategy: Test the 3D tilt effect on service cards for smoothness. Verify the service filtering works and animations are correct. For case studies, check the flip animation and ensure the lightbox gallery is fully functional (opens, closes, navigates).

subtasks.title: Create Services Section Shell and Data Model
subtasks.description: Create the main 'ServicesSection' component file and add it to the homepage. Define the data structure for services, including properties like title, description, icon, and category, in a new data file.
subtasks.details: Create `apps/web/src/components/sections/services-section.tsx`. Define a `Service` type and create an array of service objects in `apps/web/src/lib/data/services.ts`. Import and render `<ServicesSection />` in `apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/page.tsx` after the existing `<FeaturesSection />`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify that the `ServicesSection` component renders its title and a placeholder on the homepage. Ensure the service data file is created and exports the data correctly.

subtasks.title: Develop Interactive 3D Tilt Service Card Component
subtasks.description: Build the 'ServiceCard' component that displays service data and implements a 3D tilt effect on mouse hover using Framer Motion hooks.
subtasks.details: Create a new component `apps/web/src/components/cards/service-card.tsx`. Use Framer Motion's `useMotionValue` for `x` and `y`, and `useTransform` to map mouse position over the card to `rotateX` and `rotateY` CSS properties. The card should be styled using Tailwind CSS and accept a service object as a prop.
subtasks.testStrategy: Render the `ServiceCard` in isolation (e.g., in Storybook or a test page). Move the mouse over the card to confirm the 3D tilt effect is smooth and visually correct. Check that the card content displays properly.

subtasks.title: Implement Service Category Filtering with Animations
subtasks.description: Add category filter buttons to the 'ServicesSection'. Implement state management to track the active filter and use Framer Motion's 'AnimatePresence' to animate the filtering of service cards.
subtasks.details: In `services-section.tsx`, add a list of buttons for each service category. Use the `useState` hook to manage the active category state. Filter the services array based on the state. Wrap the mapped `ServiceCard` components in `<AnimatePresence>` and apply `initial`, `animate`, and `exit` props to the cards for a smooth fade/slide animation.
subtasks.testStrategy: On the homepage, click different category filter buttons. Verify that the list of services updates correctly. Ensure that cards for the old category animate out and cards for the new category animate in smoothly.

subtasks.title: Create Case Studies Section with Flippable Cards
subtasks.description: Build the 'CaseStudiesSection' and a 'CaseStudyCard' component that flips on hover to reveal more details. This includes defining the data model for case studies.
subtasks.details: Create `apps/web/src/components/sections/casestudies-section.tsx` and add it to `page.tsx`. Create `apps/web/src/components/cards/casestudy-card.tsx`. Use Framer Motion to animate `rotateY` on hover to create the flip effect. The card will have a 'front' (e.g., title, image) and a 'back' (e.g., description, 'view more' button). Define the case study data structure in `apps/web/src/lib/data/casestudies.ts`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify the Case Studies section renders on the homepage. Hover over a `CaseStudyCard` to ensure the flip animation is smooth and correctly reveals the back content. Test on multiple browsers.

subtasks.title: Implement Lightbox Gallery for Case Study Images
subtasks.description: Develop a modal-based lightbox gallery that opens when a 'CaseStudyCard' is clicked. The gallery should allow navigation between multiple images and include a Before/After slider component for comparison images.
subtasks.details: Create a reusable `LightboxGallery.tsx` component in `apps/web/src/components/ui/`. This component will accept an array of images/content and a starting index. Clicking a `CaseStudyCard` will open this lightbox. Integrate a third-party or custom 'Before/After' image comparison slider (e.g., `react-before-after-slider`) as a possible slide type within the gallery.
subtasks.testStrategy: Click on a case study card to verify the lightbox opens. Check that you can navigate between images using next/previous buttons. Confirm the 'Before/After' slider is interactive and works as expected. Ensure the lightbox can be closed.

tasks.title: Create Testimonials Section with 3D Carousel
tasks.description: Build the testimonials section featuring a 3D rotating carousel for cards, support for video testimonials, and an auto-scrolling customer logo marquee.
tasks.details:
1. **3D Carousel**: Implement a carousel where cards are positioned in 3D space. This can be achieved with a library like `embla-carousel-react` combined with CSS transforms, or a custom implementation using Framer Motion's `useTransform` on a scroll progress value to rotate the carousel. Add touch/swipe support and autoplay functionality that pauses on hover. 
2. **Video Testimonials**: Integrate a simple video player within a card, potentially opening the video in the main modal component on click. 
3. **Logo Marquee**: Create a component that infinitely scrolls a list of customer logos using a CSS animation on the `transform: translateX` property.
tasks.testStrategy: Test the 3D carousel on desktop (mouse drag) and mobile (touch swipe). Verify autoplay and pause-on-hover functionality. Ensure video testimonials can be played. Check that the logo marquee is a seamless, continuous loop.

subtasks.title: Scaffold Testimonials Section and Card Components
subtasks.description: Create the main `Testimonials.tsx` section component and a reusable `TestimonialCard.tsx` component. Define the data structure and types for the testimonial content, and render a static list of cards.
subtasks.details: Create a new file `Testimonials.tsx` inside `apps/web/src/components/sections/`. Create a `TestimonialCard.tsx` component, potentially within a new `apps/web/src/components/testimonials/` directory. Define a TypeScript interface for testimonial data, including fields like `author`, `quote`, `company`, `avatarUrl`, and an optional `videoUrl`. Populate `Testimonials.tsx` with mock data and render a static list of styled `TestimonialCard` components using the existing `Card` from `/ui` as a base.
subtasks.testStrategy: Confirm that the `Testimonials` section component renders correctly on the main page. Verify that a static list of testimonial cards is displayed with the correct mock data and styling.

subtasks.title: Implement 3D Carousel Core Logic with Framer Motion
subtasks.description: Develop the core drag-to-rotate functionality for the 3D testimonial carousel using Framer Motion, focusing on the physics and 3D transformations.
subtasks.details: Within `Testimonials.tsx`, use Framer Motion's `motion` components. Utilize `useMotionValue` to track the carousel's rotation and `useTransform` to map the scroll/drag position to a `rotateY` value. Apply dynamic `transform` styles to each `TestimonialCard` based on its index in the array to position it in a 3D circle. Implement drag controls using `drag='x'` on the main carousel container.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test the drag interaction on a desktop with a mouse and on a mobile device with touch. Verify that the carousel rotates smoothly and the cards are positioned correctly in 3D space according to the drag input.

subtasks.title: Add Autoplay, Navigation, and Final Styling to Carousel
subtasks.description: Enhance the 3D carousel with an autoplay feature that pauses on hover, add navigation controls, and apply the final 3D perspective styling.
subtasks.details: Add a `perspective` style to the carousel's parent container in CSS to enable the 3D effect. Implement an autoplay mechanism using a `useEffect` hook with a `setInterval` that animates the motion value. Use Framer Motion's `onHoverStart` and `onHoverEnd` props on the carousel to pause and resume the autoplay. Optionally, add clickable dot or arrow indicators to navigate between testimonials.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify that the carousel autoplays smoothly. Confirm that hovering the mouse over the carousel pauses the animation and it resumes correctly on mouse out. Test that any navigation controls successfully switch to the intended testimonial.

subtasks.title: Integrate Video Player into Cards via Global Modal
subtasks.description: Enable video testimonials by adding a play button to relevant cards. Clicking the button will trigger the existing global modal component to open and play the video.
subtasks.details: In `TestimonialCard.tsx`, conditionally render a play icon if the testimonial data includes a `videoUrl`. Attach an `onClick` handler to this icon. This handler will use the context or hook associated with the `Modal.tsx` component from `apps/web/src/components/ui/` to open the modal and pass the video content (e.g., a React component containing an `iframe` or `<video>` tag with the `videoUrl`) to be rendered inside it.
subtasks.testStrategy: Click the play icon on a card with a video URL and verify the modal opens. Ensure the video loads correctly inside the modal and is playable. Confirm that cards without a video URL do not display the play icon.

subtasks.title: Create Auto-Scrolling Customer Logo Marquee
subtasks.description: Build a separate, infinitely scrolling marquee component to display a list of customer logos below the main testimonials carousel.
subtasks.details: Create a new component `LogoMarquee.tsx` in `apps/web/src/components/sections/`. Inside, map over a list of logo image URLs. Use CSS keyframe animations on the `transform: translateX` property to create a continuous scrolling effect. To achieve a seamless loop, render the list of logos twice and animate the container to reset its position once the first list has scrolled completely out of view.
subtasks.testStrategy: Ensure the logo marquee scrolls at a constant, smooth speed without any stuttering. Verify that the loop is seamless, with no visible jump when the animation resets. Check responsiveness to ensure it works on various screen widths.

tasks.title: Develop Content Page Templates and Components
tasks.description: Create templates and specialized components for the secondary content pages, including Services Detail, Case Study Detail, and the About page.
tasks.details:
1. **Services Detail Page**: Build an animated FAQ accordion using Framer Motion's `AnimatePresence`. Create a 'Process Timeline' component with scroll-triggered animations for each step. Design a responsive pricing table with hover effects on each tier. 
2. **Case Study Detail Page**: Implement a hero section with a video background option and animated project stat counters. 
3. **About Page**: Create a team grid with individual member cards that reveal bios on hover. Build a 'Company Story' component that animates paragraphs and milestones into view on scroll.
tasks.testStrategy: Create dynamic routes (e.g., `/services/[slug]`) and test that each template renders correctly with mock data. Verify all interactive components on these pages (accordion, timeline animations, hover effects) work as expected. Ensure pages are responsive.

tasks.title: Build Multi-Step Contact Form and Live Chat
tasks.description: Implement the primary conversion tools: a multi-step contact form with real-time validation and a floating live chat widget.
tasks.details:
1. **Multi-Step Form**: Use `react-hook-form` for state management and validation. Create a parent component to manage the current step (`useState`). Use Framer Motion's `AnimatePresence` to create smooth slide transitions between steps. For each field, provide real-time validation feedback with animated error/success states. On successful submission, route the user to an animated 'Thank You' page. 
2. **Live Chat**: Implement a floating action button with a pulse animation to draw attention. On click, a chat window slides in from the bottom/side. This can be a placeholder UI initially, with integration for a third-party service (like Intercom or Crisp) to follow.
tasks.testStrategy: Test the form end-to-end. Try submitting with invalid data to check all validation messages. Ensure step transitions are smooth. Verify successful submission redirects to the correct page. Test the live chat button's animations and the chat window's slide-in/out behavior.

tasks.title: Finalize Performance Optimization and Accessibility Audit
tasks.description: Conduct a comprehensive review of the entire application to meet the performance (<2s load, >95 Lighthouse) and accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA) requirements before launch.
tasks.details:
1. **Performance**: Run Lighthouse audits and address all reported issues. Ensure all images are optimized using `next/image` (which defaults to WebP). Analyze the bundle size with `@next/bundle-analyzer` and apply dynamic imports (`next/dynamic`) where needed. Set up caching policies for static assets. 
2. **Accessibility (A11y)**: Use automated tools like `axe-core` and manual testing for a full WCAG 2.1 AA audit. Ensure all interactive elements are keyboard-navigable. Add appropriate ARIA labels and roles. Check color contrast ratios. Implement a `prefers-reduced-motion` check to disable non-essential animations for users who request it.
tasks.testStrategy: The test is the audit itself. The task is complete when Lighthouse scores for Performance, Accessibility, and SEO are all >90 (ideally >95 for Performance). Manually tab through the entire site to ensure all controls are focusable and usable. Use a screen reader (e.g., VoiceOver, NVDA) to navigate key user flows.

subtasks.title: Install Auditing Tools and Generate Initial Performance & Accessibility Reports
subtasks.description: Install `@axe-core/react` for accessibility testing and run the existing `@next/bundle-analyzer` to generate initial reports. Run a baseline Lighthouse audit for all key pages to establish a performance benchmark.
subtasks.details: Run `npm install @axe-core/react --save-dev`. Configure `next.config.mjs` to enable the bundle analyzer by running the build with `ANALYZE=true npm run build`. Integrate `@axe-core/react` to log issues to the console during development, possibly in `src/app/layout.tsx` under a `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'` check. Document the initial Lighthouse scores for Performance, Accessibility, and SEO.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify that `axe-core` logs accessibility violations in the browser console during development. Confirm that the bundle analyzer report (`.next/analyze/`) is generated after the build. Store the initial Lighthouse reports for later comparison.

subtasks.title: Optimize Bundle Size with Dynamic Imports and Convert Images
subtasks.description: Based on the bundle analysis from the first task, identify large components or libraries and implement code-splitting using `next/dynamic`. Audit the entire codebase for native `` tags and convert them to use the `next/image` component.
subtasks.details: Review the bundle analyzer report to find candidates for dynamic import, such as heavy client-side components. Refactor these using `next/dynamic(() => import(...))`. Search the project for ``, ensuring `width`, `height`, and `alt` props are correctly set. This is critical for performance and CLS scores.
subtasks.testStrategy: After implementation, run the bundle analyzer again to confirm a reduction in the initial chunk size. Visually inspect all pages with updated images to ensure they load correctly and without layout shift. Run a Lighthouse audit to check for improvements in LCP and CLS metrics.

subtasks.title: Perform Manual Accessibility Audit for Keyboard and Screen Reader Navigation
subtasks.description: Manually test the entire application's keyboard navigability. Ensure all interactive elements are focusable, have a visible focus state, and are logically ordered. Use a screen reader (e.g., VoiceOver, NVDA) to navigate key user flows and identify issues.
subtasks.details: Using only the keyboard, tab through every page and interactive component (modals, dropdowns, forms). Verify that the focus order is logical and predictable, and that focus is properly trapped in modals. Document all issues, such as inaccessible controls or confusing navigation paths discovered with a screen reader.
subtasks.testStrategy: Create a checklist of all interactive elements and user flows. Mark each item as passed or failed for keyboard-only navigation. Use a screen reader and confirm that all content is read out logically and all controls are clearly announced and operable. The task is complete when the checklist is fully passed.

subtasks.title: Remediate ARIA Roles, Color Contrast, and Semantic HTML
subtasks.description: Address accessibility issues identified by `axe-core` and manual testing. Add necessary ARIA roles and attributes, adjust color combinations to meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast ratios, and refactor non-semantic HTML elements.
subtasks.details: Use browser dev tools to inspect and correct ARIA roles and properties on custom components (e.g., add `role='button'` to a clickable div, or `aria-label` to an icon-only button). Use a color contrast checker to validate all text against its background, fixing any instances that fail the 4.5:1 ratio. Replace `div` or `span` elements used for interaction with semantic `<button>` or `<a href="...">` tags.
subtasks.testStrategy: Re-run the `axe-core` audit to ensure it reports zero critical violations. Manually verify fixes for issues found during the manual audit. Use a color-picker browser extension to confirm that text and background color pairs meet or exceed a 4.5:1 contrast ratio.

subtasks.title: Implement Asset Caching Policies and `prefers-reduced-motion` Check
subtasks.description: Finalize performance and accessibility by configuring caching for static assets in `next.config.mjs` and implementing a system-wide check for the `prefers-reduced-motion` media query to disable non-essential animations.

Create a utility or use a global CSS media query to detect `(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`. Apply this to disable `framer-motion` animations on components like buttons and cards.

In OS/browser settings, enable the 'reduce motion' option and verify that animations across the site are disabled. Conduct a final Lighthouse audit to confirm performance scores are >95.

tasks.title: Implement Core Email Notification System with NodeMailer
tasks.description: Create a robust and resilient email service using NodeMailer within the Express.js API for sending transactional emails, featuring a queuing system and fallback SMTP provider support.
tasks.details:
1. **Installation**: Navigate to the API directory (`apps/api`) and install the required package: `npm install nodemailer`.
2. **Configuration**: The service must be configured via environment variables. Add the following to your `.env.example` and `.env` files: `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS`, `SMTP_SECURE` (true/false), and corresponding fallback variables: `SMTP_FALLBACK_HOST`, `SMTP_FALLBACK_PORT`, etc.
3. **Service Creation**: Create a new file at `apps/api/src/services/emailService.js`. Inside, initialize two nodemailer transports: a primary transport using the main SMTP variables and a `fallbackTransport` using the fallback variables.
4. **Core Function**: Implement an async function `sendEmail({ to, subject, html })`. This function should not send the email directly but instead push the email job onto an in-memory queue (e.g., a simple array) for asynchronous processing.
5. **Queue Processing**: Implement a queue consumer function that processes jobs from the in-memory queue. For each job, it will `try` to send with the primary transport. If that fails, it will `catch` the error, log it, and then attempt to send using the `fallbackTransport` within a nested `try...catch`.
6. **Error Handling & Logging**: Integrate with the existing logging middleware/service. Log all major events: job added to queue, send attempt, send success (specifying which transport was used), primary transport failure, and fallback transport failure.
7. **Templating**: The `html` parameter of the `sendEmail` function should accept a complete HTML string. A separate utility can be created later to render templates into this string before calling the service.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. **Unit Tests (Jest)**: Mock the `nodemailer` library. Write tests for `emailService.js` to verify that a call to `sendEmail` correctly adds a job to the in-memory queue. Test the queue processor logic: simulate a primary transport failure and assert that the fallback transport's `sendMail` method is called.
2. **Integration Tests**: In a test environment, configure the `.env` with a real SMTP testing service like Ethereal.email or Mailtrap. Create a temporary test endpoint in the API that calls `sendEmail`. Write an integration test that hits this endpoint and verifies that an email is successfully delivered to the test inbox. 
3. **Fallback Mechanism Test**: Configure the primary SMTP credentials with invalid data and the fallback credentials with valid data. Run the integration test again and verify the email is still delivered, and the logs show the primary failure and fallback success.
4. **Manual Verification**: Use a tool like Postman to call the test endpoint and confirm email receipt in a real email client (e.g., Gmail) to check for any spam filtering issues or rendering problems.

tasks.title: Implement Database Backups and Redis Caching Layer
tasks.description: Set up automated PostgreSQL backups to ensure data safety and implement a Redis caching layer for the API to improve response times for frequently accessed data.
tasks.details:
1. **Redis Caching Implementation (in `apps/api`)**:
   - Install the `ioredis` package: `npm install ioredis`.
   - Create a Redis client singleton at `apps/api/src/config/redis.ts`. It should connect using the `REDIS_URL` environment variable.
   - Develop a generic caching service at `apps/api/src/services/cache.service.ts`. This service will provide `get`, `set`, `del`, and a `getOrSetCache` wrapper function. The wrapper will implement the 'cache-first with DB fallback' pattern and handle JSON serialization.
   - Refactor existing data-fetching services (e.g., for services, blog posts) to use the caching service. For example: `return cacheService.getOrSetCache('services:all', () => prisma.service.findMany(), 3600);`.
   - Implement automated cache invalidation. In `update` or `delete` service functions, call `cacheService.del('services:all')` and `cacheService.del(`services:${id}`).
   - Add `REDIS_URL` to `.env` and `.env.example`.
   - For diagnostics, add a simple middleware that adds a `X-Cache: HIT` or `X-Cache: MISS` header to responses.

2. **Database Backup Implementation**:
   - Create a new directory: `scripts/backup`.
   - Inside, create a `backup.sh` bash script. This script will use `pg_dump` to create a timestamped, compressed backup file. Example command: `pg_dump "$DATABASE_URL" | gzip > "$BACKUP_STORAGE_PATH/backup-$(date +%F-%H%M).sql.gz"`.
   - Create a `restore.sh` script that demonstrates restoring from a backup file to a target database.
   - The script must be configured via environment variables: `DATABASE_URL` and `BACKUP_STORAGE_PATH`.
   - Document the process for setting up a cron job to automate the daily execution of `backup.sh`. Example cron entry: `0 2 * * * /path/to/your/project/scripts/backup/backup.sh`.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. **Caching Verification**:
   - Write unit tests for `cache.service.ts` using `ioredis-mock` to verify the `get`, `set`, `del`, and `getOrSetCache` logic.
   - Perform integration tests on cached API endpoints (e.g., `GET /api/services`). The first request should be slow (cache miss), and subsequent requests should be significantly faster (cache hit). Verify the presence of `X-Cache` headers.
   - Test cache invalidation by sending a `PUT` or `DELETE` request to an endpoint, then a `GET` request to the collection endpoint to confirm the data is refreshed and not stale.
   - Use `redis-cli MONITOR` during testing to observe `GET`, `SET`, `DEL` commands and confirm the correct keys are being used.

2. **Backup Verification**:
   - Manually execute `./scripts/backup/backup.sh`. Confirm a valid, compressed `.sql.gz` file is created in the specified `BACKUP_STORAGE_PATH`.
   - Create a new, empty temporary database. Execute `./scripts/backup/restore.sh` pointing to the new backup file and the temporary database. Connect to the temp database and run queries to verify all data has been restored correctly.
   - Check logs from the backup script to ensure success and error conditions are being reported properly.

tasks.title: Develop Bitrix24 API Integration Client
tasks.description: Create a backend service in the Express API to integrate with the Bitrix24 REST API. This service will be responsible for creating new leads from contact form submissions, handling data mapping, authentication, and error reporting via email alerts.
tasks.details:
1. **Service Creation**: Create a new service file at `apps/api/src/services/bitrix24Service.js`. This service will export a method `createLead(formData)`. 
2. **Environment Configuration**: Add `BITRIX24_WEBHOOK_URL` to the `.env` and `.env.example` files in the `apps/api` directory. This URL contains the user ID and secret code for the inbound webhook.
3. **Lead Creation Logic**: Implement the `createLead` method using `axios` to send a `POST` request. The final endpoint will be `${process.env.BITRIX24_WEBHOOK_URL}/crm.lead.add.json`.
4. **Data Mapping**: Inside `createLead`, transform the contact form data (from Task 9) into the Bitrix24 lead structure. Map fields like `name`, `phone`, and `email` to the required format (e.g., `NAME`, `PHONE: [{ "VALUE": formData.phone, "VALUE_TYPE": "WORK" }]`). The lead `TITLE` should be dynamically generated, e.g., `"New Lead from Website - ${formData.name}"`. Assign a static `SOURCE_ID` like `"WEB"`.
5. **Error Handling**: Wrap the `axios` call in a `try...catch` block. On failure, log the error from the Bitrix24 API. Import the `EmailService` from Task 11 and use it to send an alert to an admin email address (defined in an env var like `ADMIN_EMAIL`). The alert should contain the lead data that failed to be created and the specific API error response.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. **Unit Tests (Jest)**: In `bitrix24Service.test.js`, mock `axios` and the `EmailService`. Write a test to verify that `createLead` calls `axios.post` with the correctly structured payload and URL. Write a second test that simulates a failed `axios` call and asserts that `emailService.sendEmail` is invoked with the appropriate error details and original lead data.
2. **Integration Test (Postman/API Test)**: Configure a test environment with valid Bitrix24 webhook credentials. Make a `POST` request to the API endpoint that triggers this service (e.g., `/api/contact-submit`) with valid sample data. Verify that a new lead appears in the Bitrix24 CRM dashboard. 
3. **Failure Test**: Send another request with invalid credentials or malformed data to the endpoint. Verify that the API returns a 5xx error and that an admin notification email is successfully sent and received.

tasks.title: Integrate Frontend Analytics with GA4 and Yandex.Metrica
tasks.description: Embed Google Analytics 4 and Yandex.Metrica tracking scripts into the Next.js frontend, implement a cookie consent mechanism, and create custom event tracking for key user interactions like page views, form submissions, and button clicks.
tasks.details:
1. **Configuration:** Add `NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_YANDEX_ID` to the environment files (`.env`, `.env.example`) in the `apps/web` directory.
2. **Cookie Consent:** Create a cookie consent banner component at `apps/web/src/components/layout/CookieConsent.tsx`. Use UI components from Task #2 (e.g., `Button`, `Card`). The banner should set a persistent cookie (e.g., `cookie_consent=true`) when the user accepts. This banner should be conditionally rendered from the root layout (`apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx`).
3. **Analytics Service:** Create a file at `apps/web/src/lib/analytics.ts`. This file will export helper functions:
   - `init()`: Checks for the consent cookie and, if present, injects the GA4 and Yandex.Metrica script tags into the document head.
   - `trackPageView(url)`: Sends a page view event to both platforms.
   - `trackEvent(eventName, params)`: Sends a custom event to both platforms (e.g., `window.gtag('event', ...)` and `window.ym(...)`).
4. **Provider Component:** Develop an `AnalyticsProvider.tsx` component in `apps/web/src/components/providers/`. This client component will use the `useEffect` hook to call the `init()` function once. It will also use the `usePathname` and `useSearchParams` hooks to call `trackPageView()` on route changes.
5. **Root Layout Integration:** Wrap the main content in `apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx` with the `AnalyticsProvider` and include the `CookieConsent` component.
6. **Event Implementation:**
   - **Form Submission:** In the multi-step contact form component from Task #9, import and call `trackEvent('form_submission', { form_id: 'contact_form' })` in the `onSubmit` success handler.
   - **Service Inquiry:** Similarly, trigger `trackEvent('service_inquiry', { service: 'requested_service_name' })` on successful form submission.
   - **Button Clicks:** Modify the core `Button.tsx` component (from Task #2) to accept an optional prop `analyticsEvent: { name: string, params: object }`. If the prop is present, add it to the `onClick` handler to call `trackEvent(name, params)`. This enables declarative event tracking across the app.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. **Consent First:** Clear all site data. On first load, verify the cookie consent banner appears and that no analytics scripts (gtag.js, metrika.js) are loaded in the browser's Network tab. 
2. **Script Injection:** Accept the cookie consent. Verify that the GA4 and Yandex.Metrica scripts are now loaded. Refresh the page and confirm the banner does not reappear and scripts load immediately.
3. **Page View Tracking:** Navigate between several pages (e.g., Home, About, Services). Using a browser extension like 'Google Analytics Debugger' or by observing network requests, confirm that a `page_view` event is sent to both analytics platforms on each route change.
4. **Form Submission Tracking:** Complete and submit the multi-step contact form from Task #9. Verify that the `form_submission` and `service_inquiry` events are captured in the analytics debugger with the correct parameters.
5. **Event Tracking:** Identify a button that has been updated for analytics tracking (e.g., a 'Learn More' button). Click it and verify the corresponding `button_click` event is fired.
6. **Real-time Verification:** Log into the Google Analytics 4 and Yandex.Metrica dashboards and check the 'Realtime' reports to ensure all tested events are appearing as they are triggered.

tasks.title: Complete v1.0 Final Testing and QA Phase
tasks.description: Execute the final testing and quality assurance phase for the v1.0 release, including Lighthouse audits, manual accessibility checks, E2E test suite setup, and deployment to a staging environment for validation.
tasks.details:
1. **Lighthouse Performance Audit**: Run the production build locally (`npm run build && npm start` in `apps/web`). Use the Lighthouse CLI (`npx lighthouse http://localhost:3000 --output html --output-path ./lighthouse-report.html --view`) to audit the application. Address any regressions since the audit in Task #10 and ensure final scores for Performance, Accessibility, and SEO are all above 90.
2. **Manual Accessibility & UX Validation**:
   - **Color Contrast**: Using browser developer tools, manually inspect key UI elements defined in the design system (Task #1), ensuring a minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio (WCAG 2.1 AA) for text on all backgrounds, including gradients.
   - **Screen Reader Testing**: With NVDA (Windows) or VoiceOver (Mac), perform a full walkthrough. Create a checklist covering navigation, the 3D carousel (Task #7), interaction with the cookie consent banner (Task #14), and successful submission of the contact form. All interactive elements must be focusable and have proper ARIA labels.
3. **End-to-End (E2E) Test Suite Setup**:
   - Install and configure Playwright in the monorepo root: `npm create playwright@latest`.
   - Configure `playwright.config.ts` to use `http://localhost:3000` as the `baseURL` and set up the `webServer` property to automatically launch the Next.js dev server.
   - Implement an initial smoke test in `apps/web/tests/smoke.spec.ts` that verifies the homepage loads and the main call-to-action is visible.
4. **API Integration Testing**:
   - In the `apps/api` directory, create a new integration test suite (e.g., `tests/integration/contact.test.js`).
   - Using `supertest` with Jest, write tests that simulate a frontend POST request to the API's contact endpoint. Mock the outbound calls to the Bitrix24 service (Task #13) and Email service (Task #11) to confirm that the API correctly processes valid form data and handles validation errors gracefully.
5. **Staging Environment Deployment**:
   - Prepare deployment configurations for `apps/web` (e.g., `vercel.json`) and `apps/api` (e.g., `Dockerfile`).
   - Deploy the web application to Vercel and the API to a suitable service like Fly.io or Heroku.
   - Configure all required environment variables in the staging provider's dashboard, including database credentials, Redis URL (Task #12), and third-party API keys (Task #13, #14).
tasks.testStrategy:
1. **Deliverables Checklist**: Create and complete a `FINAL_QA_REPORT.md` file in the project root to track all outcomes.
2. **Audit Reports**: Attach the generated `lighthouse-report.html` to the pull request. The QA report must summarize the final scores, confirming they meet the >90 target.
3. **Accessibility Validation**: In the QA report, include the completed screen reader test checklist and confirm that all color contrast requirements from WCAG 2.1 AA are met.
4. **Test Suite Confirmation**: Provide a log or screenshot of the new Playwright E2E smoke test passing. Include the code coverage report from the new API integration tests to demonstrate their execution.
5. **Staging URL**: Add the public URL of the deployed staging application to `FINAL_QA_REPORT.md` for final User Acceptance Testing (UAT).
6. **Production Readiness Sign-off**: The completed QA report will serve as the formal sign-off document, certifying that all checks have passed and the v1.0 application is ready for production.

tasks.title: Implement Dynamic Open Graph Image Generation
tasks.description: Create a dynamic Open Graph (OG) image generation service using @vercel/og to produce custom, branded images for social media sharing across all pages.
tasks.details:
1. **Setup and Configuration:**
   - In the `apps/web` directory, install the necessary library: `npm install @vercel/og`.
   - Ensure the brand's font files (e.g., Inter.otf, etc.) that support Cyrillic characters are located in `/apps/web/public/fonts/`.
   - Verify that `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` is defined in `.env.local` and other environment files, as it will be used to construct the absolute URL for the OG image.

2. **API Route Implementation:**
   - Create a new Edge Function API route at `apps/web/src/pages/api/og.tsx`.
   - The route will parse query parameters: `title` (string), `description` (string), and `type` (e.g., 'home', 'service', 'case', 'default').
   - Fetch the font data within the API route. Example: `const fontData = await fetch(new URL('../../../public/fonts/YourBrandFont-Regular.otf', import.meta.url)).then(res => res.arrayBuffer());`
   - Use a `switch` statement on the `type` parameter to select the appropriate JSX template for the image.

3. **ImageResponse Generation:**
   - Use the `ImageResponse` constructor from `@vercel/og` to generate the image.
   - Pass the selected JSX template, with props for `title` and `description`.
   - Configure the `ImageResponse` options: `{ width: 1200, height: 630, fonts: [{ name: 'YourBrandFont', data: fontData, style: 'normal' }] }`.
   - Return the response with appropriate caching headers: `headers: { 'Content-Type': 'image/png', 'Cache-Control': 'public, immutable, no-transform, max-age=31536000' }`.

4. **OG Image Templates:**
   - Create a new directory `apps/web/src/components/og/`.
   - Develop reusable React components for each template (e.g., `OgTemplateDefault.tsx`, `OgTemplateCase.tsx`).
   - Style the templates using Tailwind CSS syntax compatible with `@vercel/og` (e.g., `tw="..."`).
   - Incorporate the TB Group logo, brand colors, and the dynamic `title` and `description` text.

5. **Metadata Integration:**
   - Update the `<Head>` component in all relevant pages (e.g., `index.tsx`, `about.tsx`, `/services/[slug].tsx`, `/cases/[slug].tsx`).
   - Dynamically construct the `og:image` URL. Example:
     ```jsx
     const ogImageUrl = new URL(`${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL}/api/og`);
     ogImageUrl.searchParams.set('title', pageTitle);
     ogImageUrl.searchParams.set('type', 'service');
     // Conditionally add description if it exists
     if (pageDescription) {
       ogImageUrl.searchParams.set('description', pageDescription);
     }
     ```
   - Add `<meta property="og:image" content={ogImageUrl.toString()} />`, `<meta property="og:image:width" content="1200" />`, and `<meta property="og:image:height" content="630" />` to the head.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. **API Endpoint Verification:** Directly access the `/api/og.tsx` route in the browser with various query parameters for `title`, `description`, and `type`. Confirm that the correct image is generated for each type.
2. **Russian Text Rendering:** Test the API endpoint with Cyrillic characters in the `title` and `description` parameters to ensure the font is correctly loaded and the text renders without issues.
3. **Social Media Debugging:** Use a tool like OpenGraph.xyz or the Facebook Sharing Debugger on a deployed staging environment. Paste URLs for the homepage, a service page, and a case study page to verify that the generated OG image is correctly fetched and displayed.
4. **Cache Header Inspection:** Using browser developer tools, inspect the network request for an OG image URL. Verify that the response headers include the `Cache-Control` directive with a long `max-age` value.
5. **Fallback and Edge Cases:** Test the API endpoint without a `description` parameter to ensure the template handles it gracefully. Check that the default template is used if an invalid `type` is provided.

tasks.description: Implement hreflang meta tags across all pages to establish the site's language as Russian (ru-RU) and prepare the infrastructure for future multi-language support. This includes updating the sitemap.xml to reflect these language-specific URLs.

   - `rel="canonical"`
2. **URL Validation:** Confirm that the `href` attribute for all three tags points to the same, correct, absolute URL for the currently viewed page.

4. **External Validator:** Use an online hreflang tag checker tool to validate the implementation on a deployed staging environment. Test the homepage and at least one other page to ensure the structure is correct and free of errors.
5. **Documentation Review:** Review the `docs/internationalization.md` file for clarity, accuracy, and completeness of instructions for future developers.
